Definition: present infinitive from G1510; to exist:--am, was. come, is, X lust after, X please well, there is, to be, was.
BiblicalUsage: This is the infinitive of the verb to be, the form that says to be, and the Greek text always carries it under the heading of that verb. Jesus asks His disciples who men say that He is, and then who they say He is, and Peter answers on the mountain that it is good for them to be there. The word is the plainest in the language, and it holds the plainest question in the Gospels.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe who do you say that I am is the question every person must answer, and my answer is that He is the Christ, the Son of the living God.
